defs.def: to damage sth by pulling it apart or into pieces or by cutting it on sth sharp; to become damaged in this way 撕裂；撕碎；扯破；戳破

ex.s: When faced with such a fence, Chesterton thinks the fact that we can’t see the point of the fence is why we should not tear it down.
ex.t: 如果你认为你可以不需要这道栅栏，因为你从未见过狐狸，那么请考虑一下：正是因为这道栅栏的存在，你才从未见过狐狸。

ex.t: 然而，随着我逐渐成长，我曾经知道如此简单的世界正变得越来越复杂，我发现我需要一种逃避方式。通过打开一本小说，我可以把负担抛在脑后，进入一个美妙而神秘的世界，在那里我现在是一个新角色。在这些世界里我可以成为任何人。我不必写下发生了什么或者作者在写这本书时使用了什么技巧。我只是为了放松而读。

ex.s: If you’ve had a bad day, do you tell your parents about it, or do you hide your tears and lie that your day was “fine”?
ex.t: 如果你今天过得很糟，你会告诉父母，还是忍住眼泪、谎称自己“挺好的”？

ex.s: And there we see the Chinese players embracing, with tears of happiness in their eyes… It's a dream come true for China!
ex.t: 我们看到中国队员相拥在一起，眼里闪着幸福的泪花……这是中国的梦想成真！

defs.def: to remove sth from sth else by pulling it roughly or violently 拉掉；撕掉；拔掉；扯掉
to pull yourself/sb away by force from sb/sth that is holding you or them 挣开；拽开；夺去；揪走
to injure a muscle, etc. by stretching it too much 拉伤；拽伤

ex.s: If we’re too impetuous, we can end up tearing out things we don’t yet realise we rely upon.

defs.def: to move somewhere very quickly or in an excited way 飞跑；狂奔；疾驰
very badly affected or damaged by sth 构成形容词
to destroy sth violently, especially by pulling it to pieces 撕毁；撕碎
